basketball team|National team]]}} | FIBA_HOF_player = kirk-samuel-penney }} '''Kirk Samuel Penney''' (born 23 November 1980) is a New Zealand former professional [[basketball]] player. He is the all-time leading scorer for [[New Zealand men's national basketball team|New Zealand's national team]] and he ranks 12th all-time in points scored at the [[FIBA Basketball World Cup|FIBA World Cup]]. In 2024, he was inducted in the [[FIBA Hall of Fame]]. Penney played four years of [[college basketball]] for the [[Wisconsin Badgers men's basketball|Wisconsin Badgers]] between 1999 and 2003, where he was twice named first-team all-conference and as an all-American. He became the second New Zealander in the [[NBA]] when he appeared briefly for the [[Miami Heat]] in 2003 and the [[Los Angeles Clippers]] in 2005. He went on to play professionally in Spain, the NBA Development League, Israel, Lithuania, Germany and Turkey. He also played six seasons for the [[New Zealand Breakers]] of the Australian [[National Basketball League (Australia)|National Basketball League]] (NBL). He was named the [[NBL Most Valuable Player Award|NBL MVP]] in 2009, named to the [[All-NBL Team|All-NBL First Team]] four times, led the NBL in scoring three times and won an NBL championship with the Breakers in 2011. Penney represented New Zealand at the [[2000 Summer Olympics|Sydney]] and [[2004 Summer Olympics|Athens]] Olympics and averaged 16.9 points at the World Championships in Indianapolis in 2002 and 24.7 points at the World Championships in Turkey in 2010. ==Early life== Penney was born in [[Auckland]], New Zealand,{{cite web |title=Kirk Penney |url=http://www.uwbadgers.com/sport_news/mbb/bios/bio.aspx?id=Penney_Kirk_mbb&sport=mbb |website=uwbadgers.com |access-date=6 December 2025 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20030627142740/http://www.uwbadgers.com/sport_news/mbb/bios/bio.aspx?id=Penney_Kirk_mbb&sport=mbb |archive-date=27 June 2003}} in the [[North Shore, New Zealand|North Shore]] region.{{cite web |title=Kirk Penney |url=http://archive.fiba.com/pages/eng/fa/player/p/pid/36576/sid/6241/tid/337/tid2//_/2014_FIBA_Basketball_World_Cup/index.html |website=fiba.com |access-date=6 December 2025 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151117184250/http://archive.fiba.com/pages/eng/fa/player/p/pid/36576/sid/6241/tid/337/tid2//_/2014_FIBA_Basketball_World_Cup/index.html |archive-date=17 November 2015}} He attended [[Westlake Boys High School]] and played junior basketball for the North Harbour Basketball Association, joining their [[National Basketball League (New Zealand)|New Zealand NBL]] team, the [[Harbour Heat|North Harbour Kings]], in [[1998 New Zealand NBL season|1998]] as a 17-year-old. He earned [[New Zealand NBL Rookie of the Year Award|NZNBL Rookie of the Year]] honours that year and helped the Kings reach the grand final.[http://www.stuff.co.nz/sport/basketball/4878398/NBL-returns-to-Final-Four-finals-format NBL returns to Final Four finals format] He also played for the Kings in [[1999 New Zealand NBL season|1999]] and [[2000 New Zealand NBL season|2000]].{{cite web|url=http://www.plug.co.nz/sport/basketball/newsletter13.htm |title=Penney Goes to the US |work=plug.co.nz |date=15 April 1999 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/19991009003104/http://www.plug.co.nz/sport/basketball/newsletter13.htm |archive-date=9 October 1999}}[http://www.nzherald.co.nz/sport/news/article.cfm?c_id=4&objectid=10125449 Basketball: NBA hopeful keen to play in Tall Blacks series] ==College career== As a freshman playing for the [[Wisconsin Badgers men's basketball|Wisconsin Badgers]] during the 1999–2000 season, Penney had a minimal role under coach Dick Bennett, but still helped his team reach the [[2000 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|NCAA Final Four]] while averaging 3.7 points and 1.4 rebounds in 34 games. As a sophomore in 2000–01, he averaged 11.2 points per game and was the second-leading scorer on the team.[http://www.foxsports.com/wisconsin/story/all-bo-ryan-starting-5-kirk-penney-071514 All-Bo Ryan starting 5: Kirk Penney] As a junior in 2001–02 playing for coach Bo Ryan, Penney was the team's leading scorer. He averaged 15.1 points and 4.9 rebounds per game while shooting 45.4 percent from the field and teamed with point guard [[Devin Harris]] to guide the Badgers to a share of the Big Ten title. Penney subsequently earned first-team All-[[Big Ten]] honours in 2001–02. As a senior in 2002–03, Penney was again the team's leading scorer. He averaged 16.2 points and was second on the team with 6.0 rebounds per game, as Wisconsin won the Big Ten regular-season title outright. For his senior-year efforts, Penney earned first-team All-Big Ten honours again and was named an honorable mention All-American. His 217 career three-point field goals made ranks third in programme history.{{cite web|url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cbb/players/kirk-penney-1.html |title=Kirk Penney Stats |work=Sports-Reference.com |access-date=27 July 2015}} ==Professional career== ===NBA and Europe (2003–2007)=== Penney was not drafted in the star-studded [[2003 NBA draft]] but joined the [[Minnesota Timberwolves]] in July that year for the [[Orlando Pro Summer League]] where he led the league in three-point shooting. On 1 September 2003, he signed with the Timberwolves, but did not make the team's final roster as he was waived on 23 October prior to the start of the [[2003–04 NBA season]]. On 3 November, he signed with the [[Miami Heat]] and made his NBA debut that same day, scoring three points in 14 minutes of action against the [[Dallas Mavericks]]. Penney became the second New Zealander (after [[Sean Marks]]) to play in the NBA. The following day, he made his second appearance for the Heat, but record no stats in just four minutes of action against the [[San Antonio Spurs]].[https://www.basketball-reference.com/players/p/penneki01/gamelog/2004/ Kirk Penney 2003–04 Game Log] On 7 November, he was waived by the Heat after the team signed [[Tyrone Hill]] instead.[http://www.nba.com/heat/news/heat_signs_hill_031107.html HEAT Signs Tyrone Hill, Asks Waivers on Kirk Penney] Following his release from the Heat, Penney moved to Spain and signed with [[CB Gran Canaria|Gran Canaria]] for the rest of the 2003–04 season. In 24 [[Liga ACB]] games for Canaria, he averaged 10.6 points and 2.1 rebounds per game. In July 2004, Penney joined the Minnesota Timberwolves for the Minnesota Summer League in Minneapolis, and the [[Chicago Bulls]] for the Rocky Mountain Revenue in Salt Lake City. On 4 November 2004, he was selected with the sixth overall pick in the 2004 [[NBA Development League]] Draft by the [[Asheville Altitude]]. He had an impressive start to the 2004–05 season and earned himself an NBA call-up. On 26 December 2004, he signed with the [[Los Angeles Clippers]]. He appeared in four games for the Clippers and scored just two points.[https://www.basketball-reference.com/players/p/penneki01/gamelog/2005/ Kirk Penney 2004–05 Game Log] He was waived by the Clippers on 3 January 2005 and returned to the Asheville Altitude to play out the season and help the team win the 2005 NBA D-League championship. On 5 August 2005, Penney signed a two-year deal with [[Maccabi Tel Aviv B.C.|Maccabi Tel Aviv]] of the [[Israeli Basketball Premier League]].[http://www.maccabi.co.il/News.asp?id=565&lang=en Kirk Penney signed for two years] He was used sparingly as a shooter off the bench and helped Maccabi qualify for the Euroleague Final Four, eventually losing to CSKA Moscow in the final. Maccabi did, however, win the 2006 Premier League championship. In 19 [[Euroleague]] games for Maccabi in 2005–06, Penney averaged 3.3 points per game.[https://www.basketball-reference.com/euro/players/kirk-penney-1.html Kirk Penney Europe Stats] In October 2006, Penney signed with [[BC Žalgiris|Žalgiris Kaunas]] as an injury replacement for [[Marcelinho Machado]].[http://www.eurosport.com/basketball/euroleague/2006-2007/zalgiris-sign-penney_sto977423/story.shtml Zalgiris sign "Tall Black" Penney] After Žalgiris won the [[Lietuvos Krepšinio Lyga|Lithuanian Basketball League]] Cup, Penney parted ways with Žalgiris. On 16 February 2007, he signed with [[ALBA Berlin]] of Germany for the rest of the 2006–07 season.[https://www.albaberlin.de/news/kirk-penney-verstaerkt-die-albatrosse-4064.html Kirk Penney verstärkt die Albatrosse] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160304045159/https://www.albaberlin.de/news/kirk-penney-verstaerkt-die-albatrosse-4064.html |date=4 March 2016 }} {{in lang|de}} ===New In seven total games for the Skyforce, he averaged 22.7 points, 4.4 rebounds, 2.1 assists and 1.4 steals per game.[https://www.basketball-reference.com/dleague/players/p/penneki01d.html Kirk Penney 11.3 points, 3.3 rebounds and 1.8 assists per game. ===Illawarra Hawks (2015–2016)=== On 27 July 2015, Penney signed with the [[Illawarra Hawks]] for the [[2015–16 NBL season]].[http://www.nbl.com.au/nbl-team-news/illawarra-hawks-secure-another-former-nbl-mvp-kirk-penney/ ILLAWARRA HAWKS SECURE ANOTHER FORMER NBL MVP, KIRK PENNEY] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160304115332/http://www.nbl.com.au/nbl-team-news/illawarra-hawks-secure-another-former-nbl-mvp-kirk-penney/ |date=4 March 2016 }} In just the third game of the season on 14 October, he scored a season-high 36 points in a 96–75 win over his former team, the [[New Zealand Breakers]].[http://www.hawks.com.au/featured-news/penney-torches-new-zealand-breakers-with-36-points/ PENNEY TORCHES NEW ZEALAND BREAKERS WITH 36 POINTS] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160305221508/http://www.hawks.com.au/featured-news/penney-torches-new-zealand-breakers-with-36-points/ |date=5 March 2016 }} He didn't miss a game for the Hawks over the team's first 22 contests before a hamstring injury suffered on 17 January 2016 against the Breakers[http://www.illawarramercury.com.au/story/3670491/penney-a-long-shot-for-wildcats-showdown/ Penney a long shot for Wildcats showdown] forced him to miss four straight games. He returned to action on 6 February, scoring 28 points in a 104–97 overtime win over the [[Townsville Crocodiles]].[http://www.illawarramercury.com.au/story/3711198/hawks-book-finals-spot-in-overtime-thriller/ Hawks book finals spot in overtime thriller] He helped the Hawks finish the regular season in third place with a 17–11 win–loss record, booking themselves a semi-final clash with the second-seeded [[Perth Wildcats]]. After losing Game 1 in Perth, the Hawks took Game 2 at home to save the series, but went on to lose the deciding Game 3 in Perth, bowing out of the playoffs with a 2–1 defeat. In 27 games for the Hawks in 2015–16, Penney averaged 20.4 points, 3.0 rebounds and 3.1 assists per game. ===Return to the Breakers (2016–2018)=== On 12 April 2016, Penney signed a three-year deal with the [[New Zealand Breakers]].{{Cite web |url=http://www.nzbreakers.co.nz/featured-news/kirk-returns-home-on-three-year-deal/ |title=KIRK RETURNS HOME ON THREE YEAR DEAL |access-date=12 April 2016 }}[http://www.stuff.co.nz/sport/basketball/78819923/kirk-penney-returns-to-the-new-zealand-breakers-on-a-threeyear-deal Family, fun fuel Kirk Penney to take up three-year deal with NZ Breakers] On 7 over the [[Adelaide 36ers]].[http://www.stuff.co.nz/sport/basketball/85879897/kirk-penney-corey-webster-combine-for-49-as-breakers-overwhelm-adelaide Kirk Penney, Corey Webster combine for 49 as Breakers overwhelm Adelaide] On 6 November 2016, he scored 30 points in an 86–70 win over the [[Brisbane Bullets]].[http://www.nbl.com.au/brisbane-bullets/penney-stays-hot-bullets-beatdown/ PENNEY STAYS HOT IN BULLETS BEATDOWN] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161106124117/http://www.nbl.com.au/brisbane-bullets/penney-stays-hot-bullets-beatdown/ |date=6 November 2016 }} He appeared in all 28 games for the Breakers in 2016–17, averaging 17.3 points, 3.4 rebounds and 2.4 assists per game. The Breakers started the 2017–18 season with a 9–1 record, before dropping to 9–3 with two Round 8 defeats. In the second defeat of Round 8, Penney was held scoreless for the first time in his 174-game NBL career.[https://www.stuff.co.nz/sport/basketball/99499695/breakers-coach-backs-his-slumping-star-kirk-penney-to-refind-his-mojo Breakers coach backs his slumping star Kirk Penney to refind his mojo] On 15 December 2017, against the Adelaide 36ers in Auckland, Penney played his 150th game for the Breakers.[https://www.stuff.co.nz/sport/basketball/99910168/midseason-purgatory-for-breakers-as-they-get-dumped-late-by-storming-adelaide Mid-season purgatory for NZ Breakers as they get dumped late by storming Adelaide] The Breakers finished the regular season in fourth place with a 15–13 record. On 22 February 2018, with finals only a week away, Penney announced his decision to retire at the end of the 2017–18 season.[https://www.stuff.co.nz/sport/basketball/101668366/breakers-legend-kirk-penney-announces-his-retirement-vows-to-go-out-a-champion Breakers legend Kirk Penney announces retirement, shooting for 'fairytale' finish]{{Cite web |url=http://www.nbl.com.au/news/article/40391-kirk-penney-calls-time-on-nbl-career |title=Kirk Penney Calls Time on Legendary NBL Career |access-date=22 February 2018 |archive-date=22 February 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180222165125/http://www.nbl.com.au/news/article/40391-kirk-penney-calls-time-on-nbl-career |url-status=dead }} His final game came in the Breakers season-ending loss to Melbourne United in Game 2 of their semi-finals series; in the 88–86 overtime loss, Penney had 17 points off the bench.{{Cite web |url=http://www.nbl.com.au/news/article/40618-boone-the-ot-hero-as-melbourne-sweep-breakers |title=Boone the OT Hero as Melbourne Sweep Breakers |access-date=5 March 2018 |archive-date=6 March 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180306023027/http://www.nbl.com.au/news/article/40618-boone-the-ot-hero-as-melbourne-sweep-breakers |url-status=dead }} In 22 games in 2017–18, he averaged 10.1 points, 2.7 rebounds and 1.0 assists per game. ===Auckland Tuatara (2022)=== In August 2022, Penney came out of retirement to play for the [[Auckland Tuatara (basketball)|Auckland Tuatara]] of the New Zealand NBL in their final regular season game of the [[2022 New Zealand NBL season|2022 season]].{{cite news|last=Labuschagne|first=Reece|url=https://www.newshub.co.nz/home/sport/2022/08/basketball-kiwi-legend-kirk-penney-to-suit-up-for-auckland-tuatara-in-nbl.html|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220805105953/https://www.newshub.co.nz/home/sport/2022/08/basketball-kiwi-legend-kirk-penney-to-suit-up-for-auckland-tuatara-in-nbl.html|url-status=dead|archive-date=5 August 2022|title=Basketball: Kiwi legend Kirk Penney to suit up for Auckland Tuatara in NBL|work=[[Newshub]] |date=5 August 2022|access-date=6 August 2022}}{{cite web|url=https://men.nznbl.basketball/game-recap-saints-beat-tuatara-for-fifth-straight-win/|title=GAME RECAP: SAINTS BEAT TUATARA FOR FIFTH STRAIGHT WIN|work=nznbl.basketball|date=6 August 2022|access-date=6 August 2022}} ==Career statistics== {{NBA player statistics legend}} ===NBA=== {{NBA player statistics start}} |- | align="left" | {{nbay|2003}} | align="left" | [[2003–04 Miami Heat season|Miami]] | 2 || 0 || '''9.0''' || .167 || '''.333''' || .000 || '''.5''' || '''.5''' || '''.5''' || .0 ||''' 1.5''' |- | align="left" | {{nbay|2004}} | align="left" | [[2004–05 Los Angeles Clippers season|L.A. Penney was part of the Tall Blacks' memorable 2002 [[FIBA Basketball World Cup|World Championships]] campaign as they surprisingly finished fourth. Penney averaged 16.9 points per game and hit 45.5% of his three-point shots.{{cite web|url=http://www.fiba.com/pages/eng/fe/10/fwcm/player/p/pid/36576/sid/4728/tid/337/profile.html |title=Kirk Penney – 2010 FIBA World Championship |work=FIBA.com |access-date=27 July 2015}}{{dead link|date=September 2023|bot=medic}}{{cbignore|bot=medic}} Penney led New Zealand to victory in the [[FIBA Oceania Championship 2009|2009 FIBA Oceania Championship]], beating Australia 177–162 on aggregate, after the two-match tie was drawn 1–1.{{cite web|url=http://www.interbasket.net/news/3773/2009/08/new-zealand-wins-2009-oceania-championship/ |title=New Zealand wins 2009 Oceania Championship |work=Interbasket.net |date=25 August 2009 |access-date=18 December 2011}} Penney was influential in both games, with 23 points and 4 assists in Game 1, and a 24 points, 7 rebounds and 10 assists in Game 2, thus winning the Al Ramsay Shield. In the 2010 World Championships in Turkey, Penney was the second leading scorer with 24.7 points per game. New Zealand also went through to the elimination rounds with a 3–2 record. Penney participated for New Zealand at the [[2014 FIBA Basketball World Cup]] in Spain and averaged 10.8 points and 4.5 rebounds in six games.[https://www.fiba.basketball/basketballworldcup/2014/player/Kirk-Samuel-Penney 2014 FIBA Basketball World Cup – Kirk Penney] In May 2016, Penney retired from international basketball after a career spanning 15 years (1999–2014).[http://www.stuff.co.nz/sport/basketball/79987865/tall-blacks-setback--kirk-penney-calls-time-on-his-international-career Tall Blacks setback − Kirk Penney calls inducted into the [[FIBA Hall of Fame]].{{cite web|url=https://www.fiba.basketball/news/fiba-hall-of-fame-class-of-2024-headlined-by-reggie-miller-and-predrag-stojakovic|title=FIBA Hall of Fame Class
